name: Paracetamol
sub_category: Antipyretic & Non-Opioid Analgesic
why_this_disease_happens: Infections or tissue injuries stimulate white blood cells to release cytokines (pyrogens like IL-1, TNF-alpha). These pyrogens trigger the preoptic area of the hypothalamus to produce Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), resetting the body's natural thermostat to a higher fever setpoint, causing chills, shivering, and systemic body aches.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Crosses the blood-brain barrier to inhibit central prostaglandin synthesis and modulate descending serotonergic pain pathways. This lowers hypothalamic PGE2 levels, resetting the thermostat back to 37°C (98.6°F) and inducing vasodilation and sweating to cool the body down.
main_cause: Fever(Pyrexia,Febrile Response, Hyperpyrexia, Hyperthermia)
drug_class: Non-opioid Analgesic and Antipyretic (para-aminophenol derivative)
main_action: Central inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis within the central nervous system (likely via COX-3 or peroxidase inhibition) and activation of descending serotonergic inhibitory pathways; resets the hypothalamic thermoregulatory set-point to lower elevated body temperature.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Pyrexia (fever from viral or bacterial infections like cold, flu, dengue)
Tension headaches and mild migraine attacks
Post-immunization or vaccine-related fevers and aches
Dental pain (toothache, post-extraction discomfort)
Dysmenorrhea (mild menstrual cramps)
Osteoarthritis (first-line conservative management for mild-to-moderate joint ache)
Musculoskeletal pain (mild sprains, backaches, neck stiffness)
Post-operative pain (as part of multimodal analgesia)
how_patients_describe_symptoms: My forehead feels burning hot and my whole body is shivering.
I have a dull, throbbing band of pressure around my head and temples.
My body feels completely beaten up, sore, and achy from this fever.
My teeth and gums are throbbing after a filling or extraction.
My knees are stiff and aching after walking up the stairs.
I have a mild fever and tender arm after taking my injection.

who_can_use_it: Adults and adolescents requiring first-line fever or pain relief
Pediatric patients (using weight-appropriate syrup/drops)
Pregnant and breastfeeding individuals (widely considered the safest first-line antipyretic/analgesic under medical guidance)
Individuals with gastric ulcers, acid reflux, or bleeding tendencies who cannot tolerate NSAIDs like Ibuprofen or Aspirin
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with severe hepatic impairment or acute liver disease (absolute caution)
Chronic heavy alcohol consumers (elevated risk of fatal hepatotoxicity due to glutathione depletion)
Severely malnourished or underweight individuals (low basal hepatic glutathione reserves)
Severe chronic renal failure (requires dosage interval lengthening)
Individuals with documented hypersensitivity to paracetamol

common_side_effects: Mild nausea or transient gastrointestinal upset
Dizziness or lightheadedness (rare)
Transient elevation of liver transaminases (ALT/AST)
Allergic skin reactions, itching, or rash (uncommon)
important_cautions: Maximum daily dose for healthy adults must strictly not exceed 4000 mg (4 grams) in 24 hours, often capped at 2000-3000 mg/day in elderly or liver-compromised patients.
High risk of accidental overdose: Paracetamol is frequently combined in over-the-counter cold, flu, and cough syrups—taking multiple branded remedies simultaneously can lead to acute liver failure.

Toxicity mechanism: Overdose saturates normal glucuronidation/sulfation pathways, causing an excess of the toxic intermediate metabolite NAPQI, which depletes hepatic glutathione and triggers massive liver necrosis.
Immediate antidote for acute overdose is intravenous or oral N-acetylcysteine (NAC), most effective within 8 to 10 hours of ingestion.
Unlike NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen), Paracetamol has minimal anti-inflammatory action at standard clinical doses and will not reduce tissue swelling.

name: Paracetamol + Thiocolchicoside
sub_category: Dual Analgesic & Muscle Relaxant
main_cause: Painful Muscle Spasms with Inflammation, Acute Lumbago, Stiff Neck, Post-Traumatic Musculoskeletal Spasms
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Combination: Non-Opioid Central Analgesic (Paracetamol) + Centrally Acting Muscle Relaxant (Thiocolchicoside)
main_action: Provides dual-action somatic relief: Paracetamol centrally inhibits prostaglandin synthesis and activates descending serotonergic pain-inhibitory pathways to blunt acute pain perception, while Thiocolchicoside selectively modulates spinal GABA-A and glycinergic inhibitory pathways to stop motor neuron hyperactivity, breaking the vicious cycle of 'Pain -> Spasm -> More Pain'.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Acute lumbago (severe lower back spasms with locked mobility)
Cervical spondylosis with paraspinal muscle contracture and radiating neck stiffness (torticollis)
Acute sciatica associated with intense piriformis or paraspinal muscle spasm
Post-traumatic skeletal muscle strain, sprains, and sports injuries
Fibrositis, myofascial trigger point pain, and tension myositis
Post-surgical orthopaedic and spinal rehabilitation pain with involuntary contractures
how_patients_describe_symptoms: I bent down to lift something heavy and my lower back seized up with stabbing pain; I can barely stand or straighten my torso.
I woke up unable to turn my neck to the side, and there is a throbbing ache spreading down into my shoulder blade.
My back muscles feel like clenched, rock-hard ropes that throb every time I move.
I pulled a muscle at the gym; it's cramping uncontrollably and throbbing with pain.

who_can_use_it: Adults and adolescents aged 16 years and older experiencing painful skeletal muscle spasms and contractures
Patients needing simultaneous muscle relaxation and pain relief without the intense stomach irritation of strong NSAIDs
Short-term acute therapy patients (strictly capped at 7 days maximum duration)
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Pregnant women, women planning pregnancy, or women of childbearing potential not utilizing strict, reliable contraception (Black Box warning for Thiocolchicoside's aneugenic metabolite M2/SL59.0955)
Nursing/breastfeeding mothers (thiocolchicoside and paracetamol pass into breast milk)
Patients with epilepsy or a history of seizure disorders (Thiocolchicoside lowers the seizure threshold)
Patients with severe liver disease, acute hepatitis, or chronic alcoholism (high risk of paracetamol hepatotoxicity)
Children and adolescents under 16 years of age

common_side_effects: Drowsiness, lightheadedness, or slight daytime fatigue
Nausea, mild epigastric discomfort, and dyspepsia
Loose stools, mild diarrhea, or flatulence
Transient dizziness or vasovagal lightheadedness
Skin rash, erythema, or localized itching (uncommon)
important_cautions: Strict 7-Day Limit: Because of Thiocolchicoside's cellular aneugenicity risk (risk of chromosomal division abnormalities at higher doses), oral treatment must strictly be limited to an acute course of 7 consecutive days.

Do Not Duplicate Paracetamol: Patients must be warned NOT to take any concurrent over-the-counter cold, flu, cough syrups, or fever tablets containing paracetamol, as doing so can easily push total daily paracetamol above the 4000 mg hepatotoxicity threshold.
Seizure Risk: Use with extreme caution in patients with traumatic brain injury or a low threshold for convulsions; discontinue immediately if twitching or epileptic activity occurs.
Take with Food: While gentler on the gastric mucosa than Aceclofenac + Thiocolchicoside combinations, taking this tablet with water after food minimizes nausea and mild gastric discomfort.

name: Piroxicam (Dispersible Tablet)
sub_category: Long-Acting Oxicam Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drug
main_cause: Severe Inflammatory Arthropathies, Osteoarthritis, Rheumatoid Arthritis, Ankylosing Spondylitis, Acute Gout Flare
why_this_disease_happens: In degenerating joints or autoimmune arthritis, chronic synovial membrane irritation activates macrophages and chondrocytes to release pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, TNF-α). This upregulates Cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), producing high local concentrations of Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2). PGE2 sensitizes nociceptive pain fibers, degrades cartilage extracellular matrix, and increases microvascular permeability, causing chronic joint swelling, erythema, heat, and debilitating morning stiffness.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Provides potent, long-acting non-selective inhibition of COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes to block prostaglandin synthesis. The dispersible form dissolves rapidly in water into a micro-fine suspension, resulting in quicker gastric mucosal dispersion, accelerated systemic absorption, and rapid joint penetration. Its exceptionally long plasma half-life (~50 hours) maintains sustained anti-inflammatory and pain-suppressive levels throughout the entire day with a single daily dose.
drug_class: Oxicam Class NSAID (Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drug)
main_action: Inhibition of cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 & COX-2), leukocyte migration inhibition into inflamed joints, and mild lysosomal enzyme stabilization.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Osteoarthritis flare-ups (severe knee, hip, or vertebral degeneration)
Rheumatoid arthritis (chronic autoimmune synovial joint inflammation)
Ankylosing spondylitis (sacroiliac and spinal ligament calcification & stiffness)
Acute gouty arthritis (sudden uric acid crystal inflammation in the big toe/ankle)
Severe post-operative or post-traumatic musculoskeletal inflammation
how_patients_describe_symptoms: My knees are warm, swollen, and cracking, and it hurts intensely just trying to stand up.
My hands and wrists are completely stiff and locked every morning for over an hour.
My lower spine and hips feel frozen, like I cannot bend or twist.
My big toe suddenly became bright red, burning hot, swollen, and too painful to even touch a bedsheet.

who_can_use_it: Adults aged 18 and older requiring once-daily relief for severe, persistent inflammatory joint conditions
Patients needing faster onset of pain relief via dispersible formulation rather than conventional slow-dissolving capsules
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Active or past history of peptic ulcer disease, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, or perforation (highest GI toxicity risk among classical NSAIDs due to long half-life)
Patients with severe congestive heart failure, ischemic heart disease, or post-CABG surgery
Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or severe hepatic insufficiency
Pregnancy (especially after week 20; strictly contraindicated in the third trimester due to risk of premature ductus arteriosus closure)
Elderly patients (>65 years) without concurrent gastroprotective PPI cover (high vulnerability to silent ulcers)
Children and adolescents under 18 years

common_side_effects: Dyspepsia, epigastric burning, nausea, and abdominal cramps
Dizziness, vertigo, and tension headache
Fluid retention, peripheral ankle edema, and elevated blood pressure
Tinnitus (ringing in the ears)
Pruritus, skin rash, or mild erythema
important_cautions: Dispersible Administration Method: The tablet must be dissolved completely in a tablespoon or small glass of plain water before drinking, or swallowed with plenty of liquid immediately after meals. Never swallow dry.

High Gastrointestinal Risk: Due to its 50-hour half-life, continuous COX-1 suppression leaves the stomach lining vulnerable. It should ideally be co-prescribed with a PPI (like Omeprazole) in vulnerable individuals.
Cardiovascular & Thrombotic Risk: Prolonged or high-dose therapy increases the risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and worsening hypertension.

Serious Skin Reactions: Black Box Warning for rare but severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs), such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Discontinue immediately at the first sign of skin peeling or mucosal blisters.

name: Polmacoxib + Paracetamol
sub_category: Targeted Selective COX-2 Inhibitor & Central Antipyretic Analgesic
main_cause: Acute & Chronic Arthritic Pain Flares, Osteoarthritis with Breakthrough Pain, Post-Surgical & Dental Orthopedic Pain
why_this_disease_happens: In acute joint flares, post-operative trauma, or dental procedures, tissue injury sparks dual nociceptive pathways: locally, damaged cells activate COX-2 to generate excessive Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), causing edema, synovial microvascular dilation, and cartilage pain sensitization; centrally, incoming pain volleys travel up the spinal cord to the brain, lowering central pain thresholds and intensifying perceived pain, stiffness, and distress.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Provides simultaneous peripheral and central blockade: Polmacoxib (2 mg) binds to red blood cell carbonic anhydrase to be transported directly into inflamed joint tissues, selectively shutting down local COX-2 and clearing swelling; concurrently, Paracetamol (325 mg) crosses the blood-brain barrier to inhibit central prostaglandin synthesis and activate descending serotonergic pain-dampening pathways, providing rapid onset relief while Polmacoxib delivers sustained anti-inflammatory control.
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Combination: Targeted Selective COX-2 Inhibitor + Para-aminophenol Analgesic
main_action: Dual-action: selective peripheral COX-2 inhibition with erythrocyte-mediated joint delivery, coupled with central hypothalamic prostaglandin and pain-pathway modulation.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Osteoarthritis flare-ups with breakthrough pain (knee, hip, and lumbar spine)
Post-operative orthopedic rehabilitation and soft tissue trauma
Post-dental extraction pain and periodontal inflammation
Acute musculoskeletal strains and inflammatory backaches
Ankylosing spondylitis and persistent arthralgia
how_patients_describe_symptoms: My knee arthritis is throbbing and swollen, and standard paracetamol isn't touching the pain.
I had a dental extraction / surgery; my jaw is pounded with sharp pain and swelling.
My lower back and hips feel deeply inflamed, stiff, and painful whenever I try to get out of a chair.
Every step feels like bone rubbing on bone with continuous dull burning pain.

who_can_use_it: Adults aged 18 and older requiring dual peripheral anti-inflammatory and fast-acting central pain relief
Patients needing stronger pain coverage than standard paracetamol alone, but with fewer gastric ulcer complications than traditional non-selective NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac)
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Individuals with documented hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, Polmacoxib, or Paracetamol
Patients with severe active hepatic impairment or chronic alcohol dependence (risk of paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity)
Individuals with ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, or history of stroke/myocardial infarction
Active gastrointestinal bleeding or peptic ulcer disease
Severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min)
Pregnancy (strictly contraindicated in the third trimester due to risks of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus) and nursing mothers
Children and adolescents under 18 years of age

common_side_effects: Mild nausea, heartburn, or epigastric discomfort
Headache or transient lightheadedness
Fluid retention or mild peripheral ankle swelling
Mild transient rise in blood pressure
Loose stools or flatulence
important_cautions: Do Not Duplicate Paracetamol: Because this tablet already contains 325 mg of Paracetamol per dose, patients must strictly avoid concurrent over-the-counter cold, flu, cough, or fever medicines containing paracetamol to prevent toxic NAPQI accumulation in the liver.
Short to Medium Term Course: Typically prescribed for acute pain flares or post-surgical recovery; do not extend long-term without periodic blood pressure and liver enzyme evaluations.
Sulfa Pharmacophore Warning: Avoid use in patients with a confirmed severe allergic history to sulfa drugs.
Administration Advice: Always swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water after food to reduce potential gastric irritation.

name: Flupirtine Maleate + Paracetamol
sub_category: Neuronal Potassium Channel Opener & Central Non-Opioid Analgesic
main_cause: Moderate-to-Severe Musculoskeletal Pain with Spasm, Radicular Sciatica, Post-Operative Orthopedic Pain, Tension Myositis
why_this_disease_happens: When trauma, disc herniation, or surgical incisions injure tissue and compress nerve roots, sensory nociceptors unleash continuous electrical volleys into the dorsal horn of the spinal cord. This causes persistent calcium influx, dislodging magnesium from NMDA receptors and driving central sensitization (amplified, chronic pain). Simultaneously, hyper-excited motor neurons cause reflexive paraspinal muscle contractures (ischemic muscle knots), while inflammatory cytokines stimulate hypothalamic prostaglandin production, making the entire body feel achy, feverish, and locked in pain.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Provides a dual central pain-gate blockade: Flupirtine opens neuronal Kv7/KCNQ potassium channels, causing potassium efflux that hyperpolarizes the resting neuronal membrane. This stabilizes nerve cells, prevents NMDA-mediated central sensitization, and dampens spinal reflex arcs to loosen locked muscle spasms without muscle weakness. In parallel, Paracetamol acts centrally to inhibit prostaglandin synthesis and activate descending serotonergic inhibitory pathways, providing rapid background analgesia and resetting elevated hypothalamic temperature. Neither component inhibits gastrointestinal COX-1, protecting the stomach lining from ulceration.
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Combination: Selective Neuronal Potassium Channel Opener (SNEPCO) + Para-Aminophenol Analgesic
main_action: Spinal membrane hyperpolarization and indirect NMDA receptor blockade combined with central hypothalamic cyclooxygenase inhibition and serotonergic pain-pathway stimulation.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Acute lumbago, degenerative disc disease, and locked lower back with radiculopathy (sciatica)
Cervical spondylosis with neck rigidity and tension-type headaches
Post-operative orthopedic rehabilitation and soft-tissue surgical trauma
Musculoskeletal sprains, fibrositis, and myofascial trigger-point pain
Patients with severe NSAID-induced gastritis or peptic ulcers requiring strong dual-action pain relief
how_patients_describe_symptoms: I have electric shocks and burning pain shooting down my leg, and my lower back is locked tight.
My neck and shoulder blades are stiff as stone, triggering a throbbing band-like headache.
Traditional painkillers like ibuprofen destroy my stomach and give me heartburn, but I need something strong for this muscle and nerve pain.
Every tiny movement causes my back muscles to seize up in unbearable cramps.

who_can_use_it: Adults aged 18 and older requiring short-term, acute relief from combined somatic, neuropathic, and spasmodic musculoskeletal pain
Patients with gastric ulcers, acid reflux, or renal sensitivity who cannot safely tolerate conventional NSAIDs (Diclofenac, Naproxen)
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with active liver disease, hepatitis, cirrhosis, or pre-existing elevated serum transaminases (ALT/AST)
Chronic alcohol consumers or individuals using concurrent hepatotoxic agents (compounds risk of hepatic necrosis)
Patients with myasthenia gravis (due to flupirtine's central myorelaxant properties)
Pregnancy and breastfeeding mothers
Children and adolescents under 18 years of age

common_side_effects: Somnolence, lightheadedness, and daytime drowsiness
Fatigue, dry mouth, and mild dizziness
Nausea, mild epigastric fullness, or heartburn
Greenish or yellowish discoloration of urine (benign flupirtine metabolite chromaturia)
Transient elevation of liver transaminases
important_cautions: Compounded Hepatotoxicity Warning: Both Flupirtine (idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury) and Paracetamol (NAPQI metabolite toxicity) place metabolic demands on the liver. Treatment duration must strictly be kept as short as possible (typically limited to 7–14 days) with baseline and periodic liver function monitoring.

Do Not Duplicate Paracetamol: The tablet already supplies 325 mg of Paracetamol per dose; patients must strictly avoid taking additional OTC paracetamol, cold/flu syrups, or headache remedies to prevent fatal hepatic overload.

Sedation & Driving Alert: Flupirtine's central potassium channel opening causes noticeable drowsiness and slows motor reflexes; avoid driving, operating power tools, or combining with alcohol/sedatives during therapy.
Take with Full Glass of Water: Best taken after food to facilitate even absorption and minimize potential light nausea.

name: Paracetamol + Domperidone
sub_category: Non-Opioid Analgesic-Antipyretic & Peripheral D2-Receptor Antagonist
main_cause: Migraine-Associated Headaches with Nausea/Vomiting, Febrile Illness with Gastric Stasis, Tension Headaches with Motion/Digestive Sickness
why_this_disease_happens: During migraine attacks or severe systemic viral fevers, sympathetic tone shifts dramatically, paralyzing normal digestive peristalsis—a clinical phenomenon known as 'gastric stasis' or gastroparesis. The stomach ceases to churn, the lower esophageal sphincter relaxes, and dopamine signaling surges in the brainstem's Chemoreceptor Trigger Zone (CTZ). This induces severe nausea, retching, and sour regurgitation. Crucially, because the stomach is static, any regular oral painkiller swallowed just sits unabsorbed in the stomach, failing to treat the throbbing cranial pain while gastric acid pools and worsens vomiting.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Solves the pharmacological bottleneck through a dual synergistic action: Domperidone blocks peripheral dopamine D2 receptors in the stomach wall and CTZ, overcoming gastric stasis, tightening the lower esophageal sphincter, and rapidly driving stomach contents forward into the duodenum while halting nausea. By opening this gastric exit pathway, it forces the co-administered Paracetamol straight into the small intestine where it is rapidly absorbed into systemic circulation. Paracetamol then crosses into the central nervous system to inhibit prostaglandin synthesis and activate descending serotonergic pain-dampening pathways, relieving throbbing headache and fever quickly before vomiting can expel the dose.
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Combination: Para-Aminophenol Analgesic-Antipyretic + Peripheral Dopamine D2 Antagonist Prokinetic
main_action: Upper gastrointestinal prokinetic acceleration and CTZ antiemesis coupled with central hypothalamic cyclooxygenase inhibition and antipyresis.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Acute migraine headaches accompanied by moderate-to-severe nausea or vomiting
Viral pyrexia (flu, dengue, gastroenteritis) presenting with fever, body aches, and emetic urges
Tension headaches exacerbated by dyspepsia, biliousness, or motion sickness
Dental and post-operative pain accompanied by post-anesthetic nausea
Dysmenorrhea associated with systemic nausea and gastric discomfort
how_patients_describe_symptoms: I have a pounding, one-sided headache and whenever it hits, I feel intensely sick to my stomach and throw up.
My fever and body ache are terrible, but every time I try to swallow a plain fever tablet, I vomit it straight back up.
My head is throbbing, food is stuck like a brick in my upper stomach, and I feel nauseous every time I open my eyes to light.
I have a fever and sick stomach where I can't keep any fluids down.

who_can_use_it: Adults and adolescents (aged 12 and older, weighing ≥35 kg) experiencing pain or fever complicated by nausea, vomiting, or delayed gastric emptying
Migraine sufferers who find standalone oral painkillers ineffective due to migraine-induced gastric stasis
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with cardiac rhythm disorders, prolonged baseline QT interval (QTc > 450ms in men, > 470ms in women), or taking concurrent QT-prolonging agents (cardiac toxicity risk from Domperidone)
Patients with severe pre-existing hepatic impairment or active liver disease (risk of Paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity and impaired Domperidone clearance)
Patients with mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction, active stomach perforation, or massive gastrointestinal bleeding
Patients with prolactinoma (prolactin-secreting pituitary tumor)
Concurrent administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (Ketoconazole, Itraconazole, Clarithromycin, Erythromycin)
Severe chronic renal failure (requires dosage interval adjustment)

common_side_effects: Dry mouth (xerostomia)
Mild headache or transient lightheadedness
Abdominal cramping or loose stools (due to prokinetic peristalsis)
Transient drowsiness or daytime tiredness
Hyperprolactinemia (rare in short courses; potential breast tenderness or galactorrhea)
important_cautions: Cardiac QT Warning (Domperidone): Domperidone can block cardiac hERG potassium channels, which may lead to QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias at higher doses or in patients over 60 years. Use strictly at recommended therapeutic doses and avoid prolonged unmonitored use.

Hepatic Paracetamol Ceiling: Do NOT combine with any other paracetamol-containing syrups, cold/flu sachets, or headache powders. Total daily Paracetamol intake must strictly remain below 4000 mg (4g) to avoid lethal liver necrosis (NAPQI buildup).

Optimal Timing for Migraines: For acute migraine attacks, take the tablet at the earliest warning sign (prodrome or aura). Starting treatment early ensures the prokinetic mechanism empties the stomach before complete gastric paralysis sets in.
Short-Term Use Recommended: Primarily formulated for acute symptomatic episodes (1 to 3 days). If migraine or nausea symptoms persist beyond 48–72 hours, formal medical evaluation is required.

name: Naproxen Sodium + Domperidone
sub_category: Neurovascular COX-Inhibitor & Peripheral Dopamine D2 Antagonist
main_cause: Acute Migraine Attack with Severe Nausea/Vomiting, Throbbing Vascular Hemicrania, Migraine-Induced Gastroparesis
why_this_disease_happens: During an acute migraine cascade, trigeminovascular activation triggers the release of vasoactive neuropeptides (like CGRP and substance P), inducing neurogenic inflammation and painful vasodilation of meningeal dural vessels. Concurrently, sympathetic nervous system dysfunction causes 'migraine-associated gastric stasis' (acute gastroparesis)—the stomach stops churning and the pyloric sphincter clamps shut. Dopamine surges stimulate the Chemoreceptor Trigger Zone (CTZ) in the brainstem, causing intense nausea and vomiting. Because the stomach is paralyzed, standard oral painkillers sit trapped in gastric acid without being absorbed, rendering them useless while the throbbing headache escalates.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Delivers a targeted two-pronged pharmacological solution: Domperidone (10 mg) selectively blocks peripheral dopamine D2 receptors in the gastric wall and the CTZ. It relieves acute nausea and reactivates gastric motility, opening the pyloric sphincter to drive stomach contents forward into the duodenum. This rapid prokinetic clearing propels the co-formulated Naproxen Sodium into the upper small intestine, where it is rapidly absorbed into systemic circulation. Naproxen then provides potent, long-acting non-selective inhibition of COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes, suppressing pro-inflammatory prostaglandin synthesis, resolving neurogenic dural inflammation, and stabilizing meningeal vascular tone for sustained relief lasting 12 to 17 hours.
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Combination: Propionic Acid NSAID (Rapid-Absorbing Sodium Salt) + Peripheral D2 Dopamine Receptor Antagonist Prokinetic
main_action: Peripheral and central cyclooxygenase (COX-1 & COX-2) blockade coupled with peripheral dopamine D2-receptor antagonism, gastric emptying acceleration, and CTZ antiemesis.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Acute migraine attacks with or without aura, especially when complicated by nausea, bilious retching, or vomiting
Menstrually related migraine (MRM) attacks driven by hormonal prostaglandin surges
Severe episodic tension-type headaches complicated by dyspepsia and light/sound sensitivity
Secondary cluster-type headaches or vascular cephalalgias refractory to standalone simple analgesics
how_patients_describe_symptoms: I have a violent, throbbing, one-sided headache that pulses behind my eyeball, and every pulse makes me want to throw up.
Whenever my migraine starts, my stomach completely freezes—I feel sick, light and sound hurt my eyes, and ordinary painkillers do nothing.
My period headache is so intense with nausea that I can't keep food or water down.
I see flashing zigzag lights or blind spots, followed by nausea and blinding head pain.

who_can_use_it: Adults and adolescents (aged 12 and older, weighing ≥35 kg) requiring rapid abortive therapy for moderate-to-severe migraine attacks accompanied by nausea or gastric stasis
Patients who experience failure or delayed onset with standard oral analgesics (paracetamol, ibuprofen) during migraine attacks
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with baseline cardiac conduction abnormalities (prolonged QT interval, congenital long QT syndrome) or taking concurrent QTc-prolonging drugs (domperidone cardiac liability)
Active or recurrent peptic ulcer disease, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, or active gastritis (Naproxen COX-1 inhibition damages gastric mucosa)
Severe chronic renal failure (GFR < 30 mL/min) or acute kidney injury
Patients with Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD) / asthma (risk of severe bronchospasm)
Third trimester of pregnancy (strictly contraindicated: causes premature closure of fetal ductus arteriosus and oligohydramnios) and breastfeeding mothers
Patients with mechanical intestinal obstruction, bowel perforation, or prolactinoma

common_side_effects: Dry mouth and transient dizziness
Mild epigastric discomfort, heartburn, or acid belching
Drowsiness, fatigue, or daytime somnolence
Abdominal cramping or loose stools (due to prokinetic peristalsis)
Transient tinnitus (ringing in ears)
important_cautions: Golden Window Rule: Must be taken at the earliest onset of migraine symptoms or during the aura phase. Once the stomach becomes completely paralyzed by full-blown migraine gastroparesis, oral absorption drops dramatically.

Cardiovascular & QT Warning: Domperidone carries a low but documented risk of cardiac ventricular arrhythmias / QT prolongation (especially in patients over 60 years or with electrolyte imbalances); keep to prescribed doses and avoid continuous unmonitored use.

Gastrointestinal Mucosal Caution: Even though Domperidone accelerates gastric emptying (reducing the time Naproxen stays in the stomach), Naproxen systemically reduces mucosal protective prostaglandins. Patients with recurrent ulcers should take it with a sip of water after light food and avoid combining with other NSAIDs.

Not for Daily Prophylaxis: This combination is strictly intended as an acute abortive attack therapy (taken PRN / as needed at the onset of a headache), NOT as a daily preventive regimen. Overuse (>10–15 days a month) can trigger Medication Overuse Headache (MOH / rebound headache).

name: Paracetamol + Tramadol Hydrochloride
sub_category: Multimodal Analgesia: Atypical Centrally Acting Opioid / SNRI & Non-Opioid Antipyretic Analgesic
main_cause: Moderate-to-Severe Acute Somatic Pain, Post-Surgical Recovery, Orthopedic Bone & Joint Trauma, Refractory Sciatica, Severe Osteoarthritic Flare-Ups
why_this_disease_happens: Following extensive surgical incision, fractures, or advanced joint degeneration, tissue damage triggers two simultaneous waves of pain: rapidly firing peripheral A-delta fibers produce sharp, localized pain signals, while slower unmyelinated C-fibers drive dull, agonizing, long-lasting ache. In the spinal dorsal horn, continuous neurotransmitter release (substance P and glutamate) overwhelms natural descending inhibitory pathways. Simple non-opioid peripheral analgesics often prove inadequate against this heavy spinal pain traffic, while high doses of pure opioids risk severe respiratory depression, sedation, and rapid tolerance.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Employs rational multimodal analgesia to achieve superior synergistic pain relief at reduced, safer doses of each component: Paracetamol (325 mg) provides rapid-onset non-opioid analgesia by centrally inhibiting cyclooxygenase/peroxidase pathways and modulating descending serotonergic pain circuits. Concurrently, Tramadol HCl (37.5 mg) delivers sustained, deeper analgesia via a dual mechanism—weak-to-moderate μ-opioid (mu-opioid) receptor agonism (further amplified by its hepatic M1 metabolite) alongside neuronal reuptake inhibition of norepinephrine (NET) and serotonin (SERT) in spinal pain-damping pathways. The combination yields faster onset than Tramadol alone, deeper and longer-lasting pain relief than Paracetamol alone, and lowers the required opioid burden.
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Multimodal Combination: Para-Aminophenol Derivative + Atypical Synthetic Opioid Agonist / Monoamine Reuptake Inhibitor
main_action: Central hypothalamic prostaglandin synthesis inhibition combined with spinal μ-opioid receptor activation and descending serotonergic / noradrenergic pain pathway amplification.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Acute post-operative surgical pain (post-laparotomy, joint replacement, spinal fusion)
Orthopedic trauma, closed fractures, and severe ligament tears
Severe osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis flare-ups unresponsive to standalone NSAIDs or paracetamol
Acute radicular neuropathic pain (severe acute sciatica, cervical radiculopathy)
Post-procedural dental and maxillofacial surgical pain
Patients with severe gastrointestinal ulcers or high bleeding risk who cannot take traditional NSAIDs (Diclofenac, Naproxen, Ibuprofen)

Patients needing stronger pain control than plain paracetamol or NSAIDs, without the heavy sedation and respiratory risks associated with full-agonist opioids like morphine
Patients with active gastric ulcers, reflux, or renal sensitivity who cannot safely take NSAIDs
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with epilepsy, a history of seizure disorders, or head trauma (Tramadol lowers the seizure threshold)
Patients concurrently taking or within 14 days of taking Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors (MAOIs), or high doses of SSRIs, SNRIs, or triptans (high risk of life-threatening Serotonin Syndrome)

Severe acute respiratory depression or severe bronchial asthma

Children and adolescents under 16 years of age

Dizziness, lightheadedness, and somnolence (daytime sleepiness)
Constipation and dry mouth
Excessive sweating (diaphoresis)
Fatigue, headache, or mild confusion in elderly patients

This combination is intended strictly for short-to-medium-term acute episodes (typically 3 to 7 days). Driving and Motor Tasks: Drowsiness and blunted reflexes are common; patients must refrain from driving, operating hazardous machinery, or consuming alcohol while taking this medicine.

name: Coumarin & Warfarin (Vitamin K Antagonist Group)
sub_category: Vascular Benzopyrones & Hepatic Vitamin K Antagonists
main_cause: Systemic Thromboembolism (DVT/PE/AF/Valves) & High-Protein Interstitial Lymphedema
why_this_disease_happens: Vascular disease manifests along two distinct pathways: (1) Intravascular Clotting: Endothelial damage, venous stasis, or chaotic atrial turbulence activates prothrombinase complexes, polymerizing fibrinogen into fibrin clots that occlude deep veins or embolize to the brain and lungs. (2) Microvascular Extravasation: Compromised lymph vessels or high capillary venous pressure allow high-molecular-weight plasma proteins (albumin) to flood interstitial spaces, trapping water, driving chronic inflammatory tissue induration, and causing elephantine limb lymphedema.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Acts through two distinct structural mechanisms: (1) Warfarin (4-hydroxycoumarin) blocks the recycling of oxidized vitamin K by inhibiting VKORC1 in hepatocytes, halting gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X, thereby preventing fibrin mesh stabilization and clot propagation. (2) Pure Coumarin (1,2-benzopyrone) does not alter the clotting cascade; instead, it stimulates interstitial macrophages to produce lysosomal proteases that fragment large, trapped extracellular proteins into tiny peptides, allowing them to drain through local microcapillaries and resolving persistent interstitial swelling.
drug_class: Benzopyrone Vascular Decongestant & 4-Hydroxycoumarin Oral Anticoagulant Group
main_action: VKORC1 enzyme inhibition with clotting factor depletion (Warfarin) and macrophage-mediated extracellular proteolysis with lymphatic drainage acceleration (Coumarin).
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) prevention and therapy (Warfarin)
Stroke prophylaxis in atrial fibrillation and mechanical prosthetic heart valves (Warfarin)
Secondary chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) and stasis dermatitis (Coumarin)
Post-mastectomy and pelvic surgical high-protein lymphedema (Coumarin)
Post-thrombotic syndrome with residual swelling (integrated vascular therapy)
how_patients_describe_symptoms: My calf suddenly became red, swollen, tight, and hot, like a rock inside my muscle (DVT).
I have an irregular, fluttering heartbeat and need medication so a clot doesn't travel to my brain.
My arm or leg feels hard, thick, and swollen like a tree trunk after lymph node surgery (Lymphedema).
I have an artificial heart valve that clicks, and I must keep my blood thin so it doesn't jam.

who_can_use_it: Patients requiring targeted long-term systemic clot prevention (Warfarin)
Patients with mechanical heart valves where direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are contraindicated (Warfarin)
Patients requiring non-surgical decongestion for protein-rich lymphatic pooling (Coumarin)
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Pregnancy (Absolute Teratogen: Warfarin crosses the placenta, causing skeletal chondrodysplasia punctata and fatal fetal hemorrhage)
Patients with active major internal bleeding, intracranial hemorrhage, or malignant hypertension
Patients with severe pre-existing hepatic cirrhosis (Warfarin clearance becomes erratic; Coumarin risks idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury)
Patients unable to undergo mandatory INR blood monitoring or maintain a stable dietary intake of vitamin K
Individuals taking NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Piroxicam) concurrently due to compounded gastric hemorrhage risk

common_side_effects: Easy bruising (ecchymosis), recurrent nosebleeds (epistaxis), and bleeding gums (Warfarin)
Gastrointestinal nausea, epigastric discomfort, and loose stools (Coumarin)
Transient elevation of liver transaminases (ALT/AST)
Temporary hair thinning (alopecia)
Rare Warfarin-induced skin necrosis (due to initial transient Protein C depletion)
important_cautions: Distinct Clinical Entities: Coumarin (1,2-benzopyrone for lymphedema) must NOT be confused with 4-hydroxycoumarin anticoagulants (Warfarin). Coumarin does not reliably thin the blood, and Warfarin cannot be used casually for simple leg swelling.

INR Monitoring Rule (Warfarin): Therapy requires strict maintenance within a target INR window (typically 2.0–3.0 for DVT/AF; 2.5–3.5 for mechanical valves). Subtherapeutic levels cause clot recurrence; supratherapeutic levels (>4.5) cause fatal hemorrhage.
Dietary Vitamin K Interaction: Green vegetables (spinach, kale, broccoli) contain vitamin K1 that directly bypasses Warfarin's inhibition. Consistency in dietary intake is essential.
Hepatotoxicity Monitoring (Coumarin): Pure coumarin can form epoxide intermediates in poor CYP2A6 metabolizers; baseline and periodic liver function tests are necessary.

Reversal Protocol: Life-threatening Warfarin bleeding must be reversed rapidly with Intravenous Vitamin K1 (Phytonadione) alongside 4-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (4F-PCC) or Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP).

name: Eperisone Hydrochloride + Paracetamol
sub_category: Dual-Action Vasodilatory Myorelaxant & Central Prostaglandin Inhibitor
main_cause: Painful Skeletal Muscle Spasms with Somatic Pain, Acute Cervical Spondylosis, Lumbago, Stiff Neck (Torticollis), Post-Traumatic Muscle Knotting
why_this_disease_happens: Trauma, sudden twist, or spinal disc degeneration triggers a self-sustaining vicious loop: hyperactive alpha and gamma spinal motor neurons cause sustained, involuntary muscle contracture. This rock-hard clamping crushes localized intramuscular capillary beds, precipitating tissue ischemia (depriving the tissue of oxygen and glucose). Trapped lactic acid, substance P, and bradykinin accumulate within the under-perfused muscle, while tissue damage stimulates central COX enzymes to synthesize PGE2. This generates severe, throbbing somatic pain, which reflexively signals the spinal cord to clamp the muscle even tighter ('Pain-Spasm-Ischemia Cycle').
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Breaks all three arms of the 'Pain-Spasm-Ischemia Cycle' simultaneously: Eperisone HCl acts centrally on the brainstem and spinal cord to dampen hyperactive mono- and polysynaptic reflex arcs, releasing the muscle clamp without causing debilitating daytime sedation or general muscle weakness. Concurrently, Eperisone's peripheral calcium-channel blocking property dilates compressed microcapillaries, restoring oxygenated blood flow and flushing out stagnant ischemic toxins. Simultaneously, Paracetamol crosses into the central nervous system to inhibit prostaglandin synthesis and activate descending serotonergic pain-dampening pathways, shutting down pain signals before they can re-trigger reflex spasms. Neither drug irritates the stomach lining, making it gentle on gastric mucosa.
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Combination: Centrally Acting Piperidine Myorelaxant & Para-Aminophenol Non-Opioid Analgesic
main_action: Spinal reflex attenuation and microcirculatory vascular smooth muscle relaxation combined with central hypothalamic prostaglandin synthesis inhibition.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Acute lumbago and locked lower back with localized aching
Cervical spondylosis with paraspinal muscle contracture, stiff neck (wryneck), and occipital tension headaches
Scapulohumeral periarthritis and frozen shoulder with secondary muscle guarding
Post-traumatic skeletal muscle sprains, myofascial trigger points, and sports injuries
Patients with muscle spasms who cannot tolerate sedating relaxants (Chlorzoxazone, Methocarbamol) or gastric-irritating NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac)

My neck and traps feel like solid stone; it hurts to turn my head and I have a tension headache building up.
Other muscle relaxants make me so drowsy I can't work or drive, but my muscle knots keep throbbing with pain.
I have tight, burning muscle ropes in my shoulders that ache with continuous dull pain.

Patients needing improved blood flow to ischemic muscle knots alongside fast central analgesia
Individuals with sensitive stomachs or histories of GERD/mild ulcers who cannot safely take Aceclofenac + Thiocolchicoside combinations
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with severe active hepatic impairment, cirrhosis, or chronic alcoholism (risk of paracetamol hepatotoxicity)
Patients with severe renal failure (requires dosage adjustment or avoidance)
Individuals with documented hypersensitivity to eperisone, piperidine derivatives, or paracetamol
Pregnancy and breastfeeding mothers (safety is not established for eperisone; contra-indicated unless strictly evaluated by a specialist)
Pediatric patients under 18 years of age
Patients with myasthenia gravis or generalized severe muscular flaccidity

Mild stomach fullness, nausea, or dry mouth
Transient fatigue, limb weakness, or daytime tiredness
Loose stools or mild diarrhea
Skin itching, erythema, or rash (uncommon)
important_cautions: Do Not Duplicate Paracetamol: The tablet contains Paracetamol (usually 325 mg or 500 mg). Patients must strictly avoid taking any concurrent OTC cold/flu tablets, cough syrups, or headache remedies containing paracetamol, ensuring the total 24-hour dose does not exceed 4000 mg to prevent irreversible liver necrosis (NAPQI poisoning).

Superior Daytime Alertness vs. Other Relaxants: Unlike traditional muscle relaxants that heavily sedate patients via general CNS depression, Eperisone specifically targets pathologically hypertonic muscle spindles while sparing voluntary muscle power. However, patients should still assess their personal response before driving or operating machinery.
Take After Meals: Taking the tablet immediately after meals optimizes absorption and minimizes mild gastrointestinal upset or lightheadedness.
Avoid Alcohol: Concurrent alcohol intake can compound central nervous system depression and orthostatic lightheadedness.

name: Aceclofenac + Paracetamol + Serratiopeptidase
sub_category: Triple Fixed-Dose Combination: Preferential COX-2 NSAID, Central Analgesic & Proteolytic Fibrinolytic Enzyme
main_cause: Severe Post-Operative & Post-Traumatic Edema, Dental Extraction Pain & Swelling, Bone Fractures, Acute Osteoarthritic Synovitis, Maxillofacial & Orthopedic Injury
why_this_disease_happens: Following significant mechanical trauma, surgical cutting, or bone injury, the body initiates a tripartite pathological cascade: (1) Ruptured capillaries dump fibrin and cellular debris into interstitial spaces, creating a dense, watertight fibrin cocoon that blocks lymphatic drainage and traps fluid into tense, painful swelling (induration). (2) Local synoviocytes and fibroblasts upregulate inducible COX-2, synthesizing massive amounts of Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) which sensitizes primary nociceptors and causes intense localized heat and erythema. (3) Ascending sensory signals fire continuous volleys into the dorsal horn and hypothalamus, lowering central pain thresholds and triggering inflammatory systemic pyrexia (fever) and throbbing ache.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Provides a comprehensive, tri-vector attack against tissue injury: First, Serratiopeptidase (15 mg, enteric-coated) functions as an enzymatic scalpel, selectively cleaving trapped extravascular fibrin meshes and cellular protein aggregates, decompressing choked microcapillaries, improving fluid drainage, washing out stagnant tissue fluid, and degrading pain-inducing bradykinin. Second, Aceclofenac (100 mg) preferentially blocks peripheral COX-2 enzymes in inflamed joint and soft tissues, shutting off local PGE2 synthesis and halting cartilage degradation without severely compromising gastrointestinal prostaglandins. Third, Paracetamol (325 mg) rapidly crosses the blood-brain barrier to inhibit central prostaglandin synthesis and activate descending serotonergic pain-inhibitory pathways, providing fast-onset baseline analgesia and resetting elevated hypothalamic temperatures.
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Triple Combination: Phenylacetic Acid NSAID + Para-Aminophenol Derivative + Enteric-Coated Bacterial Proteolytic Enzyme
main_action: Synergistic extracellular fibrin mesh proteolysis, peripheral inducible COX-2 inhibition, and central hypothalamic cyclooxygenase and pain-pathway modulation.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Post-operative orthopedic rehabilitation (joint replacements, internal fixation of fractures, arthroscopic procedures)
Post-dental extractions, impaction surgeries, and severe maxillofacial soft-tissue swelling
Acute musculoskeletal sports injuries with heavy hematomas, sprains, and joint effusions
Severe osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and rheumatoid arthritis flares with tense synovial effusions
Ear, Nose, and Throat (ENT) post-surgical inflammation and acute sinusitis with thick mucopurulent exudates

My ankle is badly sprained, black-and-blue from bruising, and the swelling feels rock-hard and warm.
The surgery wound is tight, stretched with fluid, and every step sends sharp, pounding pain through the joint.
My knee is swollen tight with fluid like a balloon, making it impossible to bend or straighten.

Patients needing faster tissue drainage and antibiotic penetration at infected or surgically traumatized sites
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with established ischemic heart disease, congestive heart failure (NYHA II-IV), or prior history of stroke/transient ischemic attacks (aceclofenac cardiovascular class contraindication)
Active or recurrent peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, or perforation
Patients with severe coagulation disorders or taking therapeutic blood thinners (Warfarin, Heparin, DOACs) due to Serratiopeptidase fibrinolytic activity and NSAID platelet inhibition
Severe hepatic impairment, cirrhosis, or chronic heavy alcoholism (risk of paracetamol hepatotoxicity)
Severe renal failure (GFR < 30 mL/min)
Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease (AERD) / triad asthma
Third trimester of pregnancy (causes premature closure of fetal ductus arteriosus) and nursing mothers
Children and adolescents under 18 years of age

Diarrhea, loose stools, or flatulence
Mild dizziness, somnolence, or lightheadedness
Transient elevation of serum liver transaminases (ALT/AST)
Skin itching, erythema, or mild rash
important_cautions: Do Not Duplicate Paracetamol: The formulation already supplies 325 mg of Paracetamol per tablet. Patients must be strictly cautioned against concurrent over-the-counter paracetamol syrups, cold/flu sachets, or headache powders to avoid toxic liver necrosis (NAPQI poisoning).

Do Not Crush or Split (Enteric-Coating Integrity): Serratiopeptidase is degraded and destroyed by gastric stomach acid. The tablet must be swallowed whole with water so that the enzyme reaches the alkaline environment of the duodenum intact.

Administration Timing (Food Rule): Although standalone Serratiopeptidase is traditionally taken on an empty stomach, when co-formulated with Aceclofenac and Paracetamol, the tablet must be taken immediately after meals to protect the gastric mucosa from direct NSAID contact.

Short-Term Acute Use Only: Typically prescribed for a duration of 3 to 7 days during the acute inflammatory and swelling phase following surgery or trauma; not recommended for indefinite chronic therapy without regular cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and hepatic reviews.
Cardiovascular Caution: Long-term or high-dose therapy with aceclofenac carries thrombotic arterial risks; keep doses to the minimum effective duration.

name: Aceclofenac + Paracetamol + Trypsin-Chymotrypsin
sub_category: Triple Fixed-Dose Combination: Preferential COX-2 NSAID, Central Analgesic & Pancreatic Serine Protease Complex
main_cause: Post-Operative Orthopedic & Maxillofacial Trauma, Fractures with Hematomas, Severe Osteoarthritis with Synovial Effusion, Post-Traumatic Soft Tissue Induration
why_this_disease_happens: Extensive surgical dissection, bone fractures, or acute blunt trauma produce tissue disruption across three fronts: (1) Ruptured microvessels leak blood, plasma proteins, and fibrin into interstitial spaces, where clotting cascades cross-link fibrin into dense fibrinous barriers that trap cellular debris and red cells into dark, indurated hematomas and occlude lymphatic drainage. (2) Traumatized synoviocytes, osteoblasts, and fibroblasts express high levels of COX-2, driving sustained intra-articular Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) synthesis that causes local hyperemia, joint capsule distension, and cartilage pain sensitization. (3) Ascending nociceptive traffic excites dorsal horn second-order neurons, generating persistent central pain perception, autonomic guarding, and systemic inflammatory pyrexia (fever).
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Deploys a synergistic multimodal therapy combining enzymatic debris lysis with peripheral and central anti-inflammatory analgesia: Trypsin and Chymotrypsin (serine endopeptidases in a 6:1 ratio, 50,000 Armour Units) survive gastric transit via enteric coating, bind plasma alpha-1-antitrypsin/alpha-2-macroglobulin, and concentrate in inflamed tissue; they enzymatically cleave extravasated fibrin clots (trypsin cleaves basic lysine/arginine bonds, chymotrypsin cleaves aromatic residues), resolving trapped hematomas, opening microcapillaries, and draining protein-rich edema. Aceclofenac (100 mg) preferentially inhibits local COX-2, stopping peripheral PGE2 synthesis to clear erythema and articular swelling without severe gastrointestinal COX-1 suppression. Paracetamol (325 mg) rapidly crosses the blood-brain barrier to inhibit central prostaglandin synthesis and enhance descending serotonergic inhibitory pain pathways, delivering quick antipyresis and baseline analgesia.
drug_class: Fixed-Dose Triple Combination: Phenylacetic Acid NSAID + Para-Aminophenol Derivative + Enteric-Coated Pancreatic Serine Protease Complex
main_action: Targeted enzymatic fibrinolysis of hematomas and proteinaceous exudates combined with preferential peripheral COX-2 inhibition and central hypothalamic cyclooxygenase blockade.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Post-operative orthopedic rehabilitation (open reduction internal fixation of fractures, total knee/hip arthroplasty, tendon repairs)
Dental, maxillofacial, and reconstructive plastic surgery accompanied by heavy bruising, hematomas, and trismus
Severe sports injuries involving high-impact muscle contusions, sprains, torn ligaments, and joint effusions
Acute exacerbations of osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis with tense joint swelling and restricted range of motion
Post-traumatic soft tissue swelling with localized tissue induration and ecchymosis

After my jaw surgery, my entire cheek is swollen tight, bruised black-and-blue, and throbbing with severe pain.
I took a heavy impact during sports; my joint is filled with fluid, dark bruises, and I cannot bear any weight on it.
My broken bone cast area is pulsing with tight fluid pressure and burning aches.

Surgical and trauma patients whose recovery is delayed by persistent extravasated blood clots and tense edema at the incision or fracture site
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with established ischemic heart disease, congestive heart failure (NYHA II–IV), or a history of cerebrovascular accident / stroke (aceclofenac class cardiovascular contraindication)

Known hypersensitivity to bovine or porcine pancreatic enzymes, aceclofenac, or paracetamol
Pregnancy (contraindicated in the third trimester due to risk of premature ductus arteriosus closure) and breastfeeding mothers
Pediatric patients under 18 years of age

Loose stools, diarrhea, or flatulence
Dizziness, lightheadedness, or mild somnolence
Cutaneous hypersensitivity: itching, rash, or localized urticaria

important_cautions: Enteric Coating Integrity: The trypsin-chymotrypsin enzyme component is proteinaceous and will be rapidly denatured and inactivated by gastric hydrochloric acid and stomach pepsin. The tablet must be swallowed whole with water—never crushed, chewed, or divided.

Take Immediately After Meals: Although pure pancreatic enzymes are traditionally dosed on an empty stomach, when co-formulated in a single tablet with Aceclofenac and Paracetamol, the tablet must be taken directly after food to protect the gastric mucosal barrier from direct NSAID-induced dyspepsia.

Avoid Paracetamol Duplication: The formulation supplies 325 mg of Paracetamol per tablet; patients must strictly avoid additional over-the-counter paracetamol, cold/flu remedies, or headache powders to prevent exceeding the 4000 mg/day liver safety threshold.

Cardiovascular & Duration Limitation: Therapy should be restricted to the acute post-traumatic or post-surgical phase (typically 3 to 7 days). Prolonged or unmonitored use of aceclofenac carries arterial thrombotic risks and requires medical reassessment.

Comparison with Serratiopeptidase Formulations (e.g., Zerodol-SP): While Serratiopeptidase combinations are primarily favored for thin exudate drainage, bacterial biofilm clearance, and sinus/soft-tissue edema, Trypsin-Chymotrypsin combinations (Chymoral-AP) provide superior enzymatic efficacy in hydrolyzing dense organized hematomas, resolving deep blood bruises, and clearing post-fracture induration.

name: Bromelain + Trypsin + Rutoside Trihydrate
sub_category: Enteric-Coated Systemic Enzyme & Bioflavonoid Anti-Edematous Complex
main_cause: Post-Operative & Post-Traumatic Edema, Surgical Hematomas, Sports Contusions, Osteoarthritis Synovial Effusions, Chronic Venous Stasis Swelling
why_this_disease_happens: Following surgical incisions, fractures, or blunt impact trauma, damaged microvessels leak blood, plasma proteins, and fluid into the interstitial space. Concurrently, inflammatory cytokines loosen endothelial junctions, maintaining persistent capillary hyperpermeability. As fibrin polymerizes into a dense cross-linked barrier, it traps cellular debris and erythrocytes, forming rigid hematomas and choking off lymphatic capillary drainage. This traps water via high oncotic pressure, producing tight, tense induration and persistent pressure-induced pain.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Employs a synergistic 'digest, clear, and seal' triad: (1) Bromelain (plant cysteine endopeptidase) activates plasminogen to plasmin, breaks down fibrinous exudate, downregulates pro-inflammatory prostaglandins (PGE2), and enzymatically cleaves nociceptive bradykinin. (2) Trypsin (pancreatic serine endopeptidase) hydrolyzes basic peptide bonds (lysine/arginine) in cross-linked fibrin networks and necrotic debris, dissolving organized blood clots and reopening occluded lymphatic channels. (3) Rutoside Trihydrate (bioflavonoid) inhibits hyaluronidase and collagenase to stabilize capillary basement membranes and endothelial tight junctions, shutting off microvascular leakage and preventing newly drained interstitial spaces from refilling with fluid.
drug_class: Enteric-Coated Systemic Proteolytic Enzyme & Phlebotonic Bioflavonoid Combination
main_action: Dual enzymatic fibrinolysis and protein debris clearance (Trypsin + Bromelain) coupled with endothelial tight-junction stabilization and capillary leakage inhibition (Rutoside).
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Post-surgical edema, hematoma resolution, and wound-healing acceleration (orthopedic, plastic, and general surgery)
Post-dental extraction trauma, impactions, and maxillofacial swelling
Acute sports trauma: ligament sprains, muscle tears, and deep intramuscular contusions
Osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis joint effusions (as a non-NSAID anti-edema and anti-inflammatory adjunct)
Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) flare-ups with marked lower-extremity pitting edema and stasis dermatitis

My sprained joint is swollen tight with trapped fluid and throbbing from internal pressure.
My legs feel heavy, stiff, and puffy by evening, and ordinary pain relievers do not reduce the swelling.
My face and jaw are swollen and tender after dental or reconstructive surgery.

who_can_use_it: Adults recovering from surgery, dental procedures, or acute blunt trauma requiring accelerated clearance of hematomas and tense tissue swelling
Patients needing an anti-inflammatory and anti-edematous regimen who cannot safely tolerate conventional NSAIDs due to active peptic ulcers, chronic kidney disease, or gastritis
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with severe congenital or acquired bleeding diatheses (hemophilia, severe thrombocytopenia)
Patients receiving therapeutic systemic anticoagulants (Warfarin, Heparin, DOACs) or dual antiplatelet therapy without close specialist monitoring (compounded bleeding liability)
Patients with known hypersensitivity to pineapple/bromelain, porcine/bovine pancreatic extracts, or buckwheat/rutoside
Severe end-stage hepatic or renal impairment
Pregnancy and breastfeeding mothers (insufficient clinical safety trial data)

common_side_effects: Mild gastrointestinal symptoms: transient nausea, flatulence, stomach rumbling, or loose stools
Cutaneous allergic reactions: pruritus, erythema, or urticaria
Minor localized capillary oozing or extension of superficial bruising at high doses

Ingestion with food consumes the enzymes on dietary proteins in the intestinal lumen.

Do Not Crush or Split: Trypsin and Bromelain are protein enzymes that are denatured and rendered inactive by gastric hydrochloric acid and pepsin; tablets must remain intact until they reach the alkaline environment of the small intestine.

Non-Ulcerogenic Alternative to NSAIDs: Because this combination does not inhibit gastroprotective COX-1 enzymes, it does not induce gastric erosions or peptic ulcers, making it an option for NSAID-intolerant patients.

Pre-Surgical Discontinuation: Due to mild fibrinolytic and antiplatelet properties, discontinue therapy 48 to 72 hours prior to scheduled major elective surgical procedures to prevent capillary oozing.

name: Deflazacort
sub_category: Oxazoline Glucocorticoid Derivative (Bone & Glucose-Sparing Systemic Steroid)
main_cause: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), Severe Autoimmune Synovitis, Acute Asthma Exacerbations, Nephrotic Syndrome, Severe Cutaneous Allergies
why_this_disease_happens: In severe autoimmune diseases, chronic inflammatory arthropathies, or allergic states, hyperactive lymphocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells generate massive quantities of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, IL-2, IL-6, TNF-alpha) via transcription factors like NF-kB and AP-1. These signals trigger microvascular leakage, synovial inflammation, tissue destruction, and eosinophil/neutrophil infiltration. In genetic dystrophies like Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), absence of the structural dystrophin protein causes repeated sarcolemmal micro-tears during contraction, triggering chronic macrophage infiltration, sustained muscular necrosis, and eventual fibro-fatty replacement of motor tissue.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Functions as an oxazoline-substituted synthetic glucocorticoid prodrug: Following rapid oral absorption, it is converted by plasma esterases to its active metabolite, 21-desacetyldeflazacort. It diffuses across target cell membranes, binds intracellular glucocorticoid receptors, and translocates to the nucleus. Here, it trans-represses NF-kB and AP-1 transcription factors, halting the synthesis of pro-inflammatory cytokines, inducible COX-2, nitric oxide synthase, and adhesion molecules. Simultaneously, it upregulates lipocortin-1 (annexin A1), blocking phospholipase A2 and shutting down arachidonic acid liberation. Due to its unique oxazoline ring structure, it exhibits reduced affinity for bone osteoblast glucocorticoid receptors and minimal mineralocorticoid activity, translating to less bone calcium loss (lower osteoporosis rate), reduced glucose deregulation (lower diabetogenic risk), and minimal sodium/water retention compared to equivalent doses of prednisolone or dexamethasone.
drug_class: Synthetic Glucocorticoid (Oxazoline Derivative of Prednisolone)
main_action: Nuclear glucocorticoid receptor agonism, trans-repression of pro-inflammatory transcription factor NF-kB, upregulation of lipocortin-1, and suppression of cellular immunity with bone/glucose-sparing properties.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) in patients aged 2 years and older (FDA-approved to preserve muscle strength and delay loss of ambulation)
Severe rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) flares

Patients needing better treatment compliance through a simplified once-daily bedtime schedule

Do Not Crush, Chew, or Split (Matrix Integrity): The sustained-release (SR) hydrophilic polymer delivery mechanism depends on an intact tablet structure. Crushing or splitting causes 'dose-dumping', converting a 24-hour slow release into a massive immediate dose, provoking severe dizziness, somnolence, and ataxia.

Bedtime Administration Rule: Must be taken as a single once-daily dose at night after dinner with water. This aligns the gentle initial release curve with bedtime, assisting with restorative sleep while avoiding daytime sedation.

Sustained-Release (SR) vs Immediate-Release (IR) Advantage: IR pregabalin produces rapid plasma peaks within 1 hour that frequently cause transient dizziness, ataxia, and nausea, followed by subtherapeutic troughs. The SR formulation blunts the Cmax spike and sustains a therapeutic plateau over 24 hours, enhancing long-term compliance.

Mandatory Renal Monitoring: Pregabalin undergoes negligible hepatic metabolism and is excreted unchanged in urine. Creatinine clearance (CrCl) must be evaluated; dosing frequency or strength must be reduced in renal impairment to prevent drug accumulation, myoclonus, and encephalopathy.

Never Discontinue Abruptly: Sudden cessation carries a dual withdrawal risk: pregabalin withdrawal (insomnia, severe anxiety, sweating, risk of rebound focal seizures) and nortriptyline withdrawal (cholinergic rebound, nausea, headache). Taper gradually over at least 1 to 2 weeks.

Avoid Alcohol, Opioids, and Sedatives: Concomitant use with alcohol, opioids (e.g., tramadol), or benzodiazepines markedly compounds central nervous system and respiratory depression, significantly heightening the risk of fatal respiratory compromise.

Cardiac Baseline in Elderly Patients: Because nortriptyline possesses class Ia antiarrhythmic membrane properties, baseline and periodic ECG surveillance is advised in patients over 50 years of age or with pre-existing cardiovascular disease.

name: Hydroxychloroquine Sulfate
sub_category: Conventional Synthetic Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drug (csDMARD) & 4-Aminoquinoline Antimalarial
main_cause: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis, Discoid Lupus, Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS) Flares, Uncomplicated Malaria
why_this_disease_happens: In systemic autoimmune disorders like SLE and rheumatoid arthritis, loss of self-tolerance permits autoreactive B and T lymphocytes to produce high-affinity autoantibodies against nuclear antigens (such as anti-dsDNA and rheumatoid factor). Self-antigens form circulating immune complexes that deposit in synovial tissue, skin microvasculature, and renal glomeruli. Plasmacytoid dendritic cells and macrophages internalize these complexes into endosomes, where endosomal Toll-like receptors (chiefly TLR-7 and TLR-9) recognize self-nucleic acids. This triggers an intracellular signaling cascade (via MyD88 and NF-kB) that produces massive amounts of pro-inflammatory cytokines, type-1 interferons (IFN-alpha), and tumor necrosis factor (TNF-alpha), driving synovial inflammation, cartilage destruction, and multisystem flares.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Functions as a weak, lipophilic base that diffuses across cell membranes and concentrates inside acidic intracellular organelles: Within endosomes and lysosomes, Hydroxychloroquine becomes protonated and trapped, raising the intra-endosomal/lysosomal pH. This pH neutralization exerts dual immunomodulatory actions: (1) It prevents the acidification required for endosomal Toll-like receptors (TLR-7 and TLR-9) to cleave and bind nucleic acids, shutting down downstream transcription factors (NF-kB) and suppressing interferon-alpha, IL-1, and TNF-alpha production. (2) It impairs lysosomal proteolysis and enzymatic loading of autoantigenic peptides onto Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) Class II molecules, blunting autoantigen presentation to helper CD4+ T-lymphocytes. Unlike biological DMARDs, it dampens autoimmune signaling without causing severe systemic immunosuppression, lowering lupus flares, preserving renal function, preventing vascular thrombosis, and reducing rheumatoid synovial proliferation.
drug_class: 4-Aminoquinoline Antimalarial Derivative / Conventional Synthetic Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drug (csDMARD)
main_action: Inhibition of endosomal acidification and TLR-7/TLR-9 signaling, disruption of MHC Class II antigen presentation, and downregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines and type-1 interferons.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) - foundational lifelong therapy to control disease activity, prevent organ damage, and reduce mortality
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) - used as monotherapy in mild disease or as part of 'triple DMARD' therapy alongside Methotrexate and Sulfasalazine
Discoid lupus erythematosus (DLE) and subacute cutaneous lupus with refractory skin lesions
Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) with polyarticular course
Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) adjunct for antithrombotic and vascular endothelial protection
Treatment and chemoprophylaxis of acute uncomplicated malaria caused by chloroquine-sensitive Plasmodium species
how_patients_describe_symptoms: My hands, wrists, and finger joints are stiff, swollen, and tender for hours every single morning.
I have systemic lupus with extreme fatigue, joint pain, and a red butterfly rash spreading across my cheeks and nose whenever I go out in the sun.
My lupus flares without warning, causing feverishness, mouth ulcers, hair thinning, and chest aches when I breathe deeply.
My doctor prescribed this long-term medication to protect my kidneys and joints from being damaged by my own immune system.

Pregnant women with SLE (crucial clinical exception: HCQ is continued throughout pregnancy and lactation because stopping it triggers severe maternal lupus flares, preeclampsia, and congenital heart block)
Patients requiring a mild, non-myelosuppressive DMARD with a favorable metabolic profile (improves lipid markers and improves insulin sensitivity)
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with pre-existing maculopathy, retinal dystrophy, or visual field deficits involving the macula (irreversible retinal toxicity risk)
Patients with documented hypersensitivity to 4-aminoquinoline derivatives (hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine)
Patients with known Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency (risk of acute drug-induced hemolytic anemia)
Patients with porphyria or psoriasis (may precipitate acute severe exacerbations)
Patients with baseline prolonged QTc interval, sick sinus syndrome, or severe cardiomyopathy (arrhythmogenic risk)
Patients with severe end-stage renal disease (GFR < 30 mL/min) without substantial dosage reduction

common_side_effects: Gastrointestinal upset: nausea, abdominal cramping, loose stools, or loss of appetite (often improves over time)
Mild headache or transient lightheadedness
Cutaneous hyperpigmentation: dark grayish-blue patches on shins, forearms, palate, or face (with long-term therapy)
Skin rash, pruritus, or mild hair thinning
Transient visual accommodation difficulties (blurring upon initial therapy)

Retinal Toxicity & Weight-Based Dosing Limit: Hydroxychloroquine deposits in the retinal pigment epithelium. To prevent irreversible retinal toxicity ('bull's-eye' retinopathy) and vision loss, the daily dose must not exceed 5.0 mg/kg of actual body weight (per American Academy of Ophthalmology guidelines). Baseline dilated retinal examination with optical coherence tomography (OCT) and automated visual fields (10-2) is required within the first year, followed by annual screenings after 5 years of therapy (or earlier if high-risk).
Take with Food or Milk: Always administer with meals or a glass of milk to minimize gastrointestinal discomfort and nausea.

Delayed Therapeutic Latency (2 to 6 Months): HCQ is a slow-acting DMARD that accumulates gradually in tissue reservoirs; noticeable clinical benefits in joint stiffness and lupus rash typically take 8 to 12 weeks, with peak therapeutic effect achieved at 6 months.

Cardiac Conduction & QTc Prolongation: Hydroxychloroquine can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid concurrent use with other QTc-prolonging agents (e.g., azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, amiodarone, tricyclic antidepressants) without ECG monitoring.

Safe in Pregnancy: Unlike many other antirheumatic agents (such as Methotrexate, Leflunomide, or Mycophenolate, which are teratogenic), HCQ is safe and recommended to maintain clinical remission throughout pregnancy in lupus patients.

Hypoglycemia in Diabetics: HCQ enhances peripheral glucose utilization and decreases insulin degradation; monitor blood glucose closely in diabetic patients receiving sulfonylureas or insulin to prevent sudden hypoglycemia.

name: Prednisolone Dispersible
sub_category: Synthetic Intermediate-Acting Glucocorticoid (Rapid-Dissolution Dispersible Formulation)
main_cause: Acute Asthma Exacerbations, Pediatric Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis), Nephrotic Syndrome Relapses, Severe Allergic Angioedema, Systemic Autoimmune Flares (SLE, Rheumatoid Arthritis), Inflammatory Eye & Skin Disorders
why_this_disease_happens: In severe inflammatory or autoimmune flares, environmental allergens, viral triggers, or autoantibodies trigger massive activation of antigen-presenting cells, mast cells, and T-helper lymphocytes. Intracellular signaling cascades phosphorylate the nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kB) and activator protein 1 (AP-1) transcription complexes, translocating them into the cell nucleus. These factors bind gene promoter regions to transcribe high levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, IL-2, IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, TNF-alpha), chemokines, and inducible inflammatory enzymes (COX-2, inducible nitric oxide synthase / iNOS). This leads to extensive microvascular endothelial leakage, mucosal edema, smooth muscle bronchospasm, dense tissue eosinophil/neutrophil infiltration, and destructive autoimmune tissue inflammation.
how_this_medicine_fights_it: Exerts rapid and potent genomic and non-genomic anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive actions via the glucocorticoid receptor: Being lipophilic, Prednisolone diffuses across target cell membranes and binds high-affinity cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptors (GR-alpha). The activated drug-receptor complex dissociates from heat shock proteins and enters the nucleus to perform two primary regulatory functions: (1) Transrepression: It directly complexes with NF-kB and AP-1, preventing their transcriptional binding and shutting down the synthesis of pro-inflammatory interleukins, TNF-alpha, COX-2, and inducible nitric oxide synthase. (2) Transactivation: It upregulates anti-inflammatory genes, notably Lipocortin-1 (Annexin A1), which inhibits Phospholipase A2 (PLA2) to cut off the release of arachidonic acid and suppress downstream prostaglandins and leukotrienes. In addition, it stabilizes lysosomal membranes, inhibits capillary permeability, induces apoptosis in autoreactive lymphocytes and eosinophils, and upregulates pulmonary beta-2 adrenergic receptor density. The dispersible formulation disintegrates rapidly in a small volume of water, ensuring rapid systemic absorption and reliable weight-based dosing for pediatric, geriatric, or dysphagic patients.
drug_class: Synthetic Glucocorticoid (Intermediate-Acting Corticosteroid / Delta-1 Derivative of Hydrocortisone)
main_action: High-affinity glucocorticoid receptor activation, driving transrepression of NF-kB pro-inflammatory cytokine pathways and induction of Lipocortin-1 (Annexin A1) to halt arachidonic acid cascade signaling.
diseases_and_conditions_it_may_be_used_f: Acute severe asthma exacerbations and status asthmaticus (burst anti-inflammatory therapy)
Pediatric croup (laryngotracheobronchitis) and acute allergic airway obstruction
Nephrotic syndrome (initial remission induction and maintenance in minimal change disease)
Severe systemic hypersensitivity reactions, urticaria, drug eruptions, and contact dermatitis
Active flares of Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), and Polymyalgia Rheumatica
Ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease exacerbations
Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP) and autoimmune hemolytic anemia

My asthma suddenly flared up with severe chest tightness and wheezing that my inhaler can no longer relieve.
My joints are red-hot, stiff, and locked up from an autoimmune flare, making it impossible to step out of bed.
My face and lips swelled up suddenly with a hot, red, stinging allergic hives reaction.

Patients with dysphagia (difficulty swallowing) or young children who cannot swallow intact solid tablets (dissolves cleanly in 5 to 10 mL of water)
Patients requiring short-course oral steroid burst therapy (3 to 5 days) for acute respiratory or allergic distress
who_should_avoid_or_limit_it: Patients with untreated systemic fungal, bacterial, or active tuberculosis infections (steroid immunosuppression can cause life-threatening dissemination)
Patients with active, untreated peptic ulcer disease (high risk of gastric ulceration and gastrointestinal bleeding)
Patients with uncontrolled systemic hypertension or severe congestive heart failure (risk of sodium and water retention)

Individuals scheduled for live-attenuated viral vaccines (measles, mumps, rubella, BCG, yellow fever) during high-dose immunosuppressive courses
